documents.t: AI features arrive (video summaries and LinkedIn writing help), playback controls reach videos embedded on other sites, and every Netflix extra becomes opt-in. New: AI features. A new AI Features tab lets you summarize videos and get LinkedIn writing help. Use a small daily allowance after you sign in, bring your own OpenAI or Anthropic key, or run a local model. Every AI feature falls back to the built-in generators when AI is not available. New: controls for embedded videos. Floating controls, keyboard shortcuts and right-click actions now work on videos embedded in other websites, like YouTube or Vimeo players inside articles and courses. The extension loads into an embedded frame only when it contains a video. Improved: Netflix features are opt-in. Netflix extras are off by default, and you turn on the ones you want in Settings, on the Netflix Features tab. Existing setups were reset once. That way everyone starts from the same place. Improved: accurate Netflix watch-time and limits. Watch-time tracking and viewing limits now count only while a video is playing in a visible tab, so a background tab does not use up your daily limit. Fixed: per-site pause stays on this device. The list of sites you paused the extension on no longer syncs across devices.

The team's other apps get a permanent home in Settings, and the promotional panel comes off the top of every Settings page, so only one banner can sit above your settings. New: "More from the developer" tab. Settings has a new tab that collects the team's other apps in one place, with a logo, a short description and a link for each. Until now the list appeared only as one step of the welcome page, so skipping setup meant losing it. The list is bundled with the extension, and nothing is fetched to show it. Opening a product is not tracked. New: "More apps" in the popup. A link at the bottom of the popup opens that tab directly. Improved: a calmer Settings page. The promotional panel that sat above every Settings page moved into the new tab, so Settings opens to your settings. A banner that does appear there stands down while the "finish your setup" reminder is showing, so two are never stacked. Improved: clearer store listings. The Chrome, Edge and Firefox listings now describe which parts of the extension link to the team's other apps, and the Chrome "contains ads" question is answered: self-promotion only, with no ad network, ad SDK or tracking involved.

When the extension clears Netflix's "device isn't part of the Netflix Household" screen, Netflix hides its own player controls, so keyboard controls now take over in that case. Every keyboard shortcut can be changed. A key can belong to only one shortcut, and your shortcuts follow you when you are signed in. New: Netflix recovery controls. After the extension clears the Household screen, Netflix keeps its player controls hidden. Only then, keyboard controls switch on: Space to play or pause, ← / → for 10 seconds, Shift + ← / Shift + → for 1 minute, Ctrl + ← / Ctrl + → for 5 minutes, Ctrl + 0 to Ctrl + 9 to jump to the start or 10% to 90%, Ctrl + - to jump to 1 minute before the end, V for subtitles, B for the audio track, plus volume, mute and fullscreen. A small notice on the player tells you they are on and links to the full list. New: change any shortcut, one key per action. Every shortcut, including the new Netflix ones, can be given another key in Settings, on the Keyboard Shortcuts tab. If the key you pick already belongs to another shortcut, you are told which one, with a link that takes you to it. New: shortcuts follow you when signed in. Your key bindings are saved in this browser and, while you are signed in, to your account, so another device picks them up the next time you open Settings on it. Fixed: announcements that never appeared. Four places where the Video Controls Plus team can post announcements (the Settings banner, the popup card, the one-time card and the opt-in notification) were showing nothing. They work now. Each one reads at most 20 entries.

Netflix and LinkedIn menu actions now run at once, and Settings shows only the switches and shortcuts that do something. The website and the store descriptions were corrected to list only what the extension does today. Improved: Netflix and LinkedIn actions run straight away. Opening a panel, starting a timer, exporting or downloading from the widget or the right-click menu now happens immediately. Before, most of these only switched the feature on and asked you to reload the page. On/off switches still apply after a reload. Fixed: four LinkedIn tools that did nothing. Profile Backup, Message Export, Job Tracker and Job Alerts had a switch and a menu item and never ran. Each now performs its action from the menu. Response Tracker and Message Scheduler had no working part and were removed. Improved: Settings that only show what works. The New Features page listed 127 switches, and only five of them changed anything. It now shows those five (gesture controls, VR / 360 mode, SponsorBlock, ad accelerator, scroll-wheel volume) with the scroll-wheel options. The Netflix switches are in the Netflix section, as before. Improved: keyboard shortcuts that all do something. 64 shortcut entries that had no effect were removed from Settings. That frees their keys. The mini-mode key and the Player Overlay display option also did nothing and are gone, and the shortcut group that was titled "v10 Features" is now called Bookmarks. Ctrl + Alt + F now opens and closes the filters tab, and Ctrl + Alt + O adds a bookmark at the current moment. New: info button on two more LinkedIn panels. The post performance overlay and the quick preview card now carry the same info button as the other panels, and it explains what the panel is and how to use it. Improved: descriptions that match the extension. The website, its license catalog and the store listings named tools that are not in the extension yet. They now list only what you can use today, with the real shortcut keys and the features that need a sign-in.

Your account now lives on our website, and the extension connects to it on Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Everyone connects once after this update. An account that existed before 16.0.0 opens empty until we finish moving the old cloud data, which follows this release. Nothing saved in your browser is affected. New: connect the extension to your account. There is no sign-in inside the extension any more. Press Connect to your account, and a tab opens on vcpeai.aoneahsan.com. Sign in there with Google, check that the page and the extension show the same short code, and press Connect this browser. The code lasts 10 minutes. You do this once in each browser, and Sign out in the extension disconnects that browser only. New: accounts on Firefox. The same steps work on Firefox, where there was no working sign-in before. New: one switch for usage analytics. Settings → Privacy & Data has a Usage analytics switch. It is on by default, and it works with or without an account. Switch it off and the extension stops sending usage events, stops counting which sites, features and speeds you use, and stops the location lookup. Crash reports to Sentry have their own switch beside it, Third-Party Error Tracking. Improved: Delete All Data deletes the account. In 15.3.0 the button removed your stored files, your profile, your synced settings and your usage data, and it left your notes, your watch-later items and the account itself. It now deletes the account, the files stored under it and everything saved under it. Improved: the shared AI allowance is counted on our server. A connected account gets 3 runs a day on our key. With your own OpenAI or Anthropic key, or a local model, there is no limit from us and you do not need an account. The extension also no longer asks your browser for the identity permission. Fixed: removing a synced watch-later item. In 15.3.0, removing a video from watch later did not remove it from your account once it had synced. Removing a video, or moving it up or down the list, now works on synced items.

You can now say a note instead of typing it: on a video in the extension, and on the website and in the Android app, where Speak also fills flashcards, a report or a feature request. Every AI run now has a level, Spark, Pulse or Surge, and a new Plans page shows what each plan gives. New: Speak a note on a video. On the widget's Tools tab, press "Speak a note", record up to 2 minutes, then check the note and save it. It's pinned where the video was when you started. The first time, a tab opens so you can allow the microphone once. You can switch Speak off in Settings → AI Features. New: Speak on the website and in the Android app. Press Speak on Notes, Flashcards, Contact or Feature requests and say it instead of typing. You see what was heard and what it became. You decide what is kept. The Android app asks for the microphone only when you first press record. New: AI levels: Spark, Pulse and Surge. Every AI run now has a level. It sets how much reasoning goes into the run, and your plan decides the level you get. The Plans page lists the level each plan gets, and the popup's AI Video Summary card and Settings on the website show your level and today's runs. New: a Plans page. The new Plans page lists Free, Pro and Team, paid monthly or yearly. Every feature is on every plan, and Pro and Team raise the daily AI runs and the AI level. Choosing a plan opens the Contact page, and the Video Controls Plus team sets it up. Improved: an AI pause says until when. On Free, when AI rests for a while, the card says "AI is resting until …" with the time. Your runs are untouched. Everything else works as usual. On Pro and Team, AI keeps working all day. Improved: recordings are deleted within 24 hours. A Speak recording, its transcripts and the proposal are deleted within 24 hours, or at once when you press Discard. A recording that becomes a proposal uses 1 AI run, and a silent recording or a failed upload uses none. The Privacy Policy has the details.

The widget does a lot more now: comfort for your eyes and captions, study tools, your library, looks and zoom, voices and rooms, GIFs and clips, automatic playback, and watch parties. It also carries 16.1.0 and 16.2.0. New: comfort for your eyes and captions. Comfort (View tab) warms the picture, makes colors clearer, restyles a site's own captions and adds a reading guide. It needs no account and sends nothing. New: study tools beside the video. A Study timer runs focus rounds and breaks. New: GIFs and clips made on your device. Tools → "Capture & export" makes GIFs, clips, time-lapses, screenshot bursts and contact sheets, and "Annotate" marks screenshots. They skip protected video. New: playback that runs on its own. Playback → "Automation" blocks autoplay, keeps a per-site speed, ramps speed and sets reminders, and Settings adds "Watch limits" and "One video at a time". New: share & watch together. "Share this moment" gives a link and QR code. Watch together keeps play, pause, seeking and speed in step for up to 20 people. Everyone needs a connected account. The Settings auto-skip switches did nothing; now they press Netflix's and Prime Video's own Skip Intro, Skip Recap and next-episode buttons after your 0–2 s delay. They need a connected account. Fixed: Netflix runs its own controls. Before, Netflix pages ran the ones for X. Improved: a Docs link. Settings and the popup link the docs site. Fixed: your language at once. Spanish, French and German screens show their language from the start.

With it on, the extension stays connected for 7 days at a time, then asks you to connect again. Two-step sign-in. Keys, assistants and webhooks are on every plan, Free included. documents.t: Video Controls Plus began as "Udemy Video Playback Speed Controls", a speed control for one site, and the Video Controls Plus team builds and maintains it. Today it ships for Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

It's a browser extension. You set the speed, loop a part, and change the sound and the picture of the video on the page you are watching, from the keyboard or the widget. It works on YouTube, Netflix, LinkedIn, Udemy, Vimeo, and any other site with a standard video, and it has extra tools on YouTube, Netflix and LinkedIn.

The Video Controls Plus team writes the extension, these docs and the release notes. What changed in each release is in the changelog. The docs describe what the extension does today, and a control that needs an account says so on its page.
Use the contact page on the website. Tell us which site, which browser and which key, and we can find the problem faster.

There is no sign-in inside the extension. You create your account on vcpeai.aoneahsan.com, where you sign in with Google, and then you connect the extension to it. Connecting works the same way on Chrome, Edge and Firefox. An account that existed before 16.0.0 opens empty until we finish moving the old cloud data, which follows this release. Nothing saved in your browser is affected.

Press Connect to your account. The button is in the popup, on the account step of the welcome page and on the Account & Sync tab in Settings. A tab opens on vcpeai.aoneahsan.com. If the page asks you to sign in, press Continue with Google. Check that the page and the extension show the same code. If the codes are different, press Cancel. Press Connect this browser. The extension shows the connection within a few seconds while the popup or Settings stays open, and otherwise within about 30 seconds. The code lasts 10 minutes. If you closed the tab, press Open the page again in the extension. Troubleshooting covers what to do when connecting fails.

The YouTube and LinkedIn extras that are on by default run without an account, and only the Settings tab where you switch them asks you to connect.

Connected, the extension stores your account data and your settings, and while the Usage analytics switch is on it records which sites, features and speeds you used. The full list is in Privacy and permissions.

Connect the extension to your account. Open the Account & Sync tab in Settings and turn on Enable Cloud Sync. Your settings are uploaded when you turn it on. Your speeds, key bindings and site settings are synced. The tab shows the last sync time. Bookmarks saved while connected sync to your account separately from this settings switch; bookmarks made while signed out remain in that browser. Button What it does Upload to Cloud Saves the settings on this device to your account Load from Cloud Replaces the settings on this device with the copy in your account Newer settings win: when two browsers save to the same account, the account keeps the newer copy. Settings you changed on this device and did not upload are overwritten by Load from Cloud. Another device picks up your keyboard shortcuts the next time you open Settings on it, but the list of sites you paused does not sync. It stays on the device where you paused them.

Sign out, in the popup or on the Account & Sync tab, disconnects this browser only. Your account stays, and so does every other browser you connected. To connect this browser again, press Connect to your account.

Open Settings, go to the Privacy & Data tab, and click Delete All Data on the Your Data card. It deletes the account itself, the files stored under it and everything saved under it. It cannot be undone. The button needs a connected account, because it deletes what is stored with your account. Export My Data is on the same card. It downloads your data as a JSON file. It also needs a connected account. You can also delete your account from the website's data deletion page when you are signed in there.

documents.t: Open the Data Management tab in Settings. Export Settings downloads your settings as a JSON file. You choose whether to include video memory and filter presets. Import Settings restores from a file you exported: Replace All replaces your current settings, and Merge keeps your current values where the file has none.

On the website, Account → Security adds a code from your phone after Google. With it on, a connected extension is trusted for 7 days, then asks you to connect again. Removing a browser there signs the extension out on it. Details: Two-step sign-in. Account → Other apps gives your own tools a way into your library: access keys for scripts, Claude or ChatGPT, and webhooks for your server. See Video Controls Plus for developers.

Every feature works on Free. Pro raises your daily AI runs and your AI level, for one person, and Team does the same for each member. The prices are on Plans. To get Pro, sign in on the website, open Plans and press Upgrade to Pro, monthly or yearly. You pay on Polar's checkout page, and Pro starts on your account as soon as Polar confirms the payment. Polar emails you a link to its customer portal, where you can cancel, change your card and download invoices. Cancel any time. Your plan runs to the end of the period you paid for. Team is set up with us: press Choose Team on Plans, which opens the contact page. Plans are bought on the website only, never inside the extension or the Android app. For anything else about your account, use the contact page.

Video Controls Plus has three AI features: a summary of a YouTube video made from its captions, writing help on LinkedIn, and Speak, which turns what you say into a note. Each runs only when you start it. Your own key or a local model needs no account, and the Shared allowance and Speak need a connected account. Open the popup on a YouTube watch page and press Summarize this video. Writing help starts on LinkedIn (LinkedIn page). Every playback control works without AI.

documents.t: Pick one on the AI provider card, in Settings → AI Features. Option on the card What you need Where your text goes Shared allowance A connected account To the Video Controls Plus server, which sends it to Anthropic. Your OpenAI key or Your Anthropic key Your API key, no account Straight from your browser to that provider Local (Ollama) Ollama on your machine Nowhere. It stays on your device. A summary, a LinkedIn writing-help answer or a Speak proposal uses 1 of your plan's daily runs on the Shared allowance, and the popup's AI card shows how many you've used today. Each plan's daily runs and its AI level (Spark, Pulse or Surge) are on Plans. On Free, AI sometimes pauses. The card says "AI is resting until …", your runs are untouched, and everything else works. On Pro and Team the run goes to a second provider instead, and your own key and a local model have no limit from the team.

Say it, then check what was written before anything is saved. Speak is in three places: The extension: Speak a note on the widget's Tools tab, on any video. It pins the note at that moment of the video. The website: Notes, Flashcards, Contact and Feature requests. The Android app: the same four pages. A recording is up to 2 minutes. The first time, the extension opens a page, "Allow the microphone for Speak", to ask once. A recording where nothing was heard, or that failed to upload, uses no run. Speak works on the Shared allowance only.

Feature What is sent Video summary The caption or transcript text of the video LinkedIn writing help The text you are drafting Speak Your recording, to our server, which sends the audio for a transcript and then only the transcripts to the AI (see Three ways to run it) While you record, your browser's own speech recognition may also send your voice to your browser's maker. The video itself is never sent.

Your recording, its transcripts and the proposal are deleted within 24 hours, or at once when you press Discard, and if our file storage cannot be reached at that moment, the audio file is removed at the next hourly check. For a summary or writing help, the team does not store the text you send or the answer. For each Shared allowance run, the server keeps a usage record for 13 months, without your text, and a count of today's runs. A key you add stays in your browser and goes only to its provider. Without AI, a summary falls back to the extension's built-in generator, with no model. The microphone and everything else are on Privacy and permissions.

Your Video Controls Plus library can be reached from outside the extension, by tools you connect yourself: a script with an access key, an assistant such as Claude or ChatGPT, or your own server hearing about each change through a webhook. You set all three up on the website, in Account → Other apps, on every plan, Free included. Each key, assistant or webhook reaches only the parts you tick for it, and acts as you. It never sees anything you couldn't see on the website yourself.

You want Use Page A script, a spreadsheet sync or a phone shortcut that reads or changes your library An access key and the REST API Access keys, The API To ask Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code or Cursor about your notes and flashcards The assistant address (MCP) Assistants Your server told the moment you save a note or a bookmark A webhook address Webhooks

Only what you tick, and only your own: Read and change your bookmarks, notes, collections and the videos in them, flashcards, learning paths and their videos, watch later, transcripts, settings and the browsers the extension is connected on. Read and remove your watch history. Only the extension adds to it, while Watch History is on. Read your screenshots. Removing one stays in the extension. Delete, when you tick Delete for that part. A key deletes straight away. A delete an assistant asks for waits on the website for your yes. Read only: watch parties you host or joined, community site fixes, and feature requests with your votes. Always readable: your plan, its limits and what you used today.
documents.s: What an outside app can reach

documents.t: Whatever you tick, no key, assistant or webhook can: reach anyone else's library, or say who else is in your watch party; host or join a watch party, vote, post a site fix or change a feature request; see your sign-in, two-step codes, recovery codes, keys or signing secrets; change your plan, payments or email, or connect the extension; read your voice notes, AI history, payments, referrals or usage analytics; open a staff page.

What Address REST API https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1 OpenAPI document https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1/openapi.json The same, as Markdown https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1/openapi.md Assistant (MCP) address https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp The OpenAPI document is built from the same list of parts and fields as the API itself, so it never describes a route the API lacks.

Free Pro Team (each member) Access keys 5 25 50 API and assistant requests a day 5,000 50,000 100,000 Webhook addresses 3 20 40 Assistant connections 3 10 25 Requests a day count every key and assistant of yours together, and start again at midnight UTC. Each key or assistant also has its own limit of 120 requests a minute, so a runaway script stops itself. Other apps shows what you have used against your plan. Plans and prices are on Plans.

A key or a webhook signing secret is shown in full once, when you make it. After that, we show it again only within ten minutes of signing in, and with a code from your authenticator when two-step sign-in is on. A browser left open can't hand one out. We email you each time a key is made, an assistant is connected or a webhook address is added. The email never contains the key or the secret.
documents.s: Keys and secrets stay hidden until you sign in again

documents.t: Access keys: make, show, replace and remove a key, and what each tick reaches. The API: requests, pages of results, errors, limits, and every part with a curl example. Assistants: connect Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code or Cursor. Webhooks: every event, what a message carries, and how to check its signature. Two-step sign-in: a code after Google, on the website and for the extension. Developers changelog: what changed for developers, newest first.

An access key works like a password for one tool: a study-sheet sync, a script, a phone shortcut. The tool sends it with each request to the API, and the key reaches only the parts of your library you ticked when you made it. Keys look like vcp_pat_ followed by a long random string. Keep a key out of anything you share.

On the website, open Account → Other apps and press Make a key. Give it a Name, so you know which tool uses it, like "Study sheet sync". Tick what it can reach. Each part has three boxes: Read, Change and Delete. Tick at least one part to read. Choose when it Stops working after: 30, 90 or 365 days, or Never. Never is allowed only for a key that only reads; a key that can change or delete always has an end date. Press Make key, then copy it. This is the one time it is shown without signing in again. Making a key needs a sign-in from the last ten minutes, and your two-step code when two-step sign-in is on. We email you that a key was made. The email never contains the key.

A tick becomes a permission on the key. The API answers 403 scope_required, naming the permission, when a key asks for something it wasn't given. Part on the website Read Change Delete What it covers in the API Bookmarks bookmarks:read bookmarks:write bookmarks:delete bookmarks Notes notes:read notes:write notes:delete notes Collections collections:read collections:write collections:delete collections, collection_videos Flashcards flashcards:read flashcards:write flashcards:delete flashcards Learning paths paths:read paths:write paths:delete learning_paths, path_videos Watch history history:read history:delete watch_history Watch later later:read later:write later:delete watch_later Transcripts transcripts:read transcripts:write transcripts:delete transcripts, transcript_texts Screenshots screenshots:read screenshots Settings and shortcuts settings:read settings:write settings Devices devices:read devices:write devices:delete devices Watch parties parties:read watch_parties, party_members Community site fixes fixes:read site_fixes Feature requests requests:read feature_requests, request_votes An empty box is a box the website doesn't offer: watch history has no change, screenshots and the shared parts are read only, and settings can't be deleted. Every key can also read your plan and today's use (account:read, the account part of the API) without a tick.

Press Show again on the key. We show it only within ten minutes of signing in, so a browser left open can't hand it out, and with your two-step code when two-step is on. A remembered browser still asks for the code here. The key stays on screen for a short while; close it when you've copied it.

Press Replace when a key may have leaked, or when you want a fresh one. You get a new key with the same name and the same parts. The key it replaced keeps working for 24 hours so you can swap it over, then it stops.

Press Remove, then press it again to confirm. The next request with that key gets "not allowed" (401 invalid_token). Nothing else changes: your library, your other keys and your assistants stay as they are.

GET /token answers with the key's kind and its permissions, sorted: curl https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1/token \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY" { "data": { "kind": "pat", "user_id": "6a1f0c52-3b7d-4e8a-9f21-0c4d5e6b7a89", "client_id": null, "scopes": ["account:read", "bookmarks:read", "notes:read", "notes:write"] } } Other apps also shows when each key was made, when it was last used and when it stops working.
documents.s: Checking what a key can do

documents.t: Free holds 5 keys, Pro 25 and Team 50 for each member. A removed key doesn't count. When you're at the limit, remove one, or move to a plan with more on Plans.

The API reads and changes your own library over HTTPS with an access key. Every address starts with: https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1 The machine-readable description is the OpenAPI 3.1 document at /openapi.json, with a Markdown copy at /openapi.md. Neither needs a key. The examples below keep the start of the address and the key in two shell variables: export VCP_API="https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/functions/v1/api/v1" export VCP_KEY="vcp_pat_..."

Send the key as a bearer token on every request, and send bodies as JSON: curl "$VCP_API/notes" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY" A token from a connected assistant works here too. A website sign-in does not: the API answers 401 and asks for an access key or an assistant's token. Each request acts as you. Our database decides every row with your own permissions, so a key can never return a row you couldn't open on the website.

One item: { "data": { "id": "0b6f3c1e-8a2d-4f5b-9c7e-1d2a3b4c5d6e", "label": "Proof of the second lemma" } } A list: { "data": [ { "id": "…" }, { "id": "…" } ], "meta": { "next_cursor": "eyJyIjoi…", "limit": 20 } } A failure: { "error": { "code": "scope_required", "message": "This credential needs the notes:write permission.", "details": { "scope": "notes:write" }, "correlation_id": "req_9c41b27d58e0f3a6" } } Times are ISO 8601. Ids are UUIDs, except where a part below says otherwise. Answers that carry your data are never cached.

Status code What happened 400 invalid_request A field, filter, sort or cursor isn't valid. details.issues lists each field. 401 invalid_token The key is missing, wrong, expired or removed. 403 scope_required The key wasn't given this permission. details.scope names it. 404 not_found Nothing at this address for this key. Another person's item looks the same as a missing one. 405 method_not_allowed This part doesn't take that method, such as a change to watch history. 409 conflict It already exists, or one of our rules refused it. The message says which. 413 payload_too_large The body is over 65,536 bytes. 429 rate_limited Too many requests. Wait for the reset time. 500 internal Something went wrong on our side. Send us the correlation_id.

A list returns 20 items unless you ask for limit, from 1 to 50. When there are more, meta.next_cursor holds a cursor; send it back as cursor with the same filters and sort to get the next page. A cursor lasts 15 minutes and works only for the query that made it. When next_cursor is null, you have everything. curl "$VCP_API/bookmarks?limit=50" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY" curl "$VCP_API/bookmarks?limit=50&cursor=eyJyIjoi…" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY" Filters are query parameters named <field>.<operator>, from the short list each part allows below: eq is equal, lte is on or before, and cs means the tags contain every value in a comma list. Sort is sort=<field>, with a leading - for newest or largest first, from the part's list; the first one listed is the default.

Each key gets 120 requests a minute. On top of that, your plan sets requests a day for all your keys and assistants together: 5,000 on Free, 50,000 on Pro and 100,000 for each Team member, starting again at midnight UTC. Every answer carries RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset (seconds), for whichever limit is closer. A 429 adds Retry-After.

DELETE needs the part's Delete tick. With an access key it removes the item at once and answers 204 with no body. With an assistant's token it removes nothing yet. It answers 202 with a link the person opens on the website to say yes, valid for ten minutes: { "data": { "status": "pending_confirmation", "confirm_url": "https://vcpeai.aoneahsan.com/developers/confirm/4e2b…", "expires_at": "2026-11-21T09:24:03.000Z" } } The extension removes it on every browser the next time it syncs, as if you had removed it there.

Every part below takes GET /<part> for a list and GET /<part>/{id} for one item, unless it says otherwise. POST /<part> makes one, PATCH /<part>/{id} changes the fields you send, and DELETE /<part>/{id} removes it. Fields not listed as yours to set are shown and never written. A video is named by four fields across these parts: platform (the site, such as youtube, netflix or linkedin), video_id (the video's own id on that site), video_url (the address of the video page) and video_title.

Moments you saved in a video: the time, a label, a note and a colour. Methods list, get, create, change, delete You set video_id, video_url and label (required), position_seconds (required, seconds from the start), platform, video_title, note, color, tags, folder Filters platform.eq, video_id.eq, tags.cs Sort -created_at Permission bookmarks curl -X POST "$VCP_API/bookmarks" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"platform":"youtube","video_id":"aircAruvnKk","video_url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aircAruvnKk","position_seconds":754,"label":"Where gradient descent starts","tags":["ml","week-3"]}' The time in the video is set when the bookmark is saved, as in the extension.

Notes you wrote at a time in a video, with a category and tags. Your flashcards from videos: front, back, tags and when each card is due. Methods list, get, create, change, delete You set video_id, video_url, front and back (required), position_seconds, platform, video_title, tags, and the review schedule: ease_factor (1.3 to 10), interval_days, repetitions, next_review_at, last_reviewed_at Filters platform.eq, video_id.eq, tags.cs, next_review_at.lte Sort next_review_at, -created_at Permission flashcards A new card is due now. Changing the review schedule is how a review is recorded, as it is in the extension. Cards due by the end of today: curl "$VCP_API/flashcards?next_review_at.lte=2026-11-21T23:59:59Z&sort=next_review_at" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY"

Methods list, get, delete Shown the video fields, video_thumbnail, video_duration_seconds, channel_name, last_position_seconds, watch_count, total_watch_seconds, first_watched_at, last_watched_at Filters platform.eq, video_id.eq Sort -last_watched_at Permission history (read and delete) curl -X DELETE "$VCP_API/watch_history/9a2c4e6f-1b3d-4f5a-8c7e-0d2f4a6b8c1e" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY"

Your watch later list, in your order, with priority and notes. Methods list, get, create, change, delete You set video_id and video_url (required), platform, video_title, video_thumbnail, video_duration_seconds, channel_name, position, priority (high, normal or low), notes Sort position, -added_at Permission later curl -X POST "$VCP_API/watch_later" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"platform":"youtube","video_id":"IHZwWFHWa-w","video_url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IHZwWFHWa-w","priority":"high"}'

transcripts lists the transcripts you saved, with language and format, newest first, and leaves the text out so a page stays small. transcript_texts reads one transcript with its text and timed lines, by the same id, or saves a new one. transcripts transcript_texts Methods list, get, delete get, create You set video_id, video_url and content (required), platform, video_title, language, language_code, is_auto_generated, format (srt, vtt, txt or json), segments Shown the video fields, language, language_code, is_auto_generated, format, file_size, downloaded_at the same, plus content and segments Sort -downloaded_at Permission transcripts transcripts curl "$VCP_API/transcript_texts/5e7a9c1b-3d5f-4a2e-9b8c-1f3a5c7e9d0b" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY" A request body is at most 65,536 bytes, so a longer transcript can't be saved from outside.

Frames you saved from videos, with the time in the video and the image size. Read only: a screenshot is removed in the extension. Methods list, get Shown the video fields, position_seconds, image_url, format (png, jpeg or webp), width, height, created_at Sort -created_at Permission screenshots (read) curl "$VCP_API/screenshots?limit=10" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY"

Your synced extension settings and keyboard shortcuts: one item, whose id is your account's. settings and keyboard_bindings are objects in the shape the extension stores them. Methods list, get, create, change You set settings, keyboard_bindings Shown settings_updated_at, keyboard_bindings_updated_at, updated_at Permission settings (read and change) The list holds your one item, or nothing before you first sync. A save keeps the newer copy, as sync between your browsers does. curl "$VCP_API/settings" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY"

Browsers the extension is connected on. They are added only by connecting the extension; here you rename or remove them. Removing one signs the extension out on that browser. Methods list, get, change, delete You set device_name Shown device_id, browser, platform, extension_version, last_seen_at, created_at Sort -last_seen_at Permission devices curl -X PATCH "$VCP_API/devices/2b4d6f8a-1c3e-4a5b-9d7f-0e2a4c6e8b1d" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"device_name":"Work laptop, Firefox"}'

These involve other people, so the API reads them and never writes them, whatever a key says. They send no webhook events. Part What it holds Filter Sort Permission watch_parties Parties you host or joined: the video, is_host, when it started, ends and ended. The join code is left out, because it is the invitation. -created_at parties:read party_members How many people are in each of your parties and when they joined. is_you marks you; nobody's name, photo or account is included, and id is a handle for the membership, not the person. party_id.eq joined_at parties:read site_fixes Player fixes people shared for websites, approved ones and your own while they wait, with is_yours. The contributor isn't named. hostname.eq -created_at fixes:read feature_requests The public board: title, description, category, status, votes and is_yours. The author isn't named. -created_at, -upvotes requests:read request_votes Your own votes: 1 up, -1 down. A vote's id is the request it is on. -created_at requests:read curl "$VCP_API/site_fixes?hostname.eq=www.coursera.org" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY"

GET /account returns one item: your plan, its AI runs a day and today's, your cloud storage and what you use of it, and other_apps, which holds your four limits from the plan table with requestsToday. Every key reads it, with no tick. curl "$VCP_API/account" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VCP_KEY"

Fields are an allowlist: a column not named on this page never leaves our database. Beyond the list in What it never reaches, that also keeps out the extension's own sync keys, the stored-file record behind a screenshot, the device that last saved your settings, and the separate sittings inside your watch history. There is no calendar feed.

Connect an assistant and you can ask it about your own library: "Which flashcards from last week's lectures are due?", "Turn my notes on this video into a summary", "Add this talk to Watch later". Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code and Cursor connect to one address: https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp The assistant sends you to the Video Controls Plus website, where you sign in, tick what it can reach and approve. It never gets a password or a key from you. The address is also on Account → Other apps, with a copy button.
In Claude, open Settings → Connectors and choose Add custom connector. Name it Video Controls Plus and paste the address above. Claude opens our website. Tick what it can reach and approve.

In ChatGPT, open Settings → Apps and connectors, then Advanced, and turn on developer mode. Choose Create, name it Video Controls Plus and paste the address above. ChatGPT opens our website. Tick what it can reach and approve.

In a terminal, run: claude mcp add --transport http video-controls-plus https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp Run /mcp inside Claude Code and choose Video Controls Plus to sign in. Your browser opens our website. Tick what it can reach and approve.

In Cursor, open Settings → Tools & MCP and choose New MCP server. Add these lines to the file it opens, then save: { "mcpServers": { "video-controls-plus": { "url": "https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp" } } } Cursor shows Needs login. Press it, tick what it can reach on our website and approve.

The approval page names the assistant and the place it returns to, then shows the same Read, Change and Delete boxes as an access key. Delete starts off. Tick at least one thing it can read, or press Deny; a denied assistant gets a "denied" answer and reaches nothing. With two-step sign-in on, you type your code to approve. A remembered browser skips the code only when the connection just reads. Letting an assistant change or delete also needs a sign-in from the last ten minutes. We email you that an assistant was connected. Whatever it reads, it reads as your own words. It never sees your sign-in, keys or anyone else's library.

An assistant never deletes anything by itself, even with Delete ticked. When you ask it to remove a note, it gets a link instead, and the request waits on the website: The assistant gives you the link, and Other apps shows it under Asked to delete, waiting for you. Open it. The page shows what would go, the video it is on, when it was asked and the time to answer by. Press Delete the note (or bookmark, card and so on), or Keep it. The request lasts ten minutes. After that nothing is deleted, and you ask the assistant again if you still want it gone. The assistant gets a "deleted" answer the next time it checks.
Each connected assistant has a line in Other apps with when it was connected and last used. Give it a name you'll recognise, or press Disconnect, then again to confirm. Its next request is refused.

Free holds 3 assistant connections, Pro 10 and Team 25 for each member. Connecting the same assistant again replaces its old approval and takes no extra place. Its requests count toward your requests a day, with your keys (limits).

Your notes, labels and card text go to the assistant as data, exactly as you wrote them. If you pasted instructions into a note, the assistant sees them as text from your library. Tick only the parts a conversation needs.
documents.s: The assistant reads your own writing

documents.t: Transport Streamable HTTP, stateless, one endpoint Sign-in OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, through our Supabase authorization server at https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/auth/v1 Discovery Protected-resource metadata at https://gjajgvsjhdbtrpvfiuwl.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource No token 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header pointing at that metadata Access keys A vcp_pat_ key works as the bearer token too, for a client you run yourself Limits 120 requests a minute per connection, plus the plan's requests a day The tools come from the same parts as the API: list_<part>, get_<part>, create_<part>, update_<part> and prepare_delete_<part>, as each part allows. tools/list shows only the tools this connection's ticks allow. The shared parts and your plan have list and get tools only, and voice notes and AI history are in no tool.
Changes for anyone building on Video Controls Plus, newest first. Product releases are in the main changelog.

New: access keys (vcp_pat_…), made on Account → Other apps, each with its own Read, Change and Delete ticks, and an end date unless it only reads. New: the API, version 1, for bookmarks, notes, collections, flashcards, learning paths, watch history, watch later, transcripts, screenshots, settings and devices, plus read-only watch parties, site fixes, feature requests and your plan. The OpenAPI 3.1 document is at /v1/openapi.json. New: the assistant address for Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code and Cursor. An assistant's delete waits on the website for your yes. New: webhooks, signed with Standard Webhooks, with 32 events to choose from and a test message, thin messages by default and Include what was written per address. New: two-step sign-in on the website, with ten recovery codes and an opt-in remembered browser for 7 days. A connected extension is trusted for 7 days with it on. Limits: Free 5 keys, 5,000 requests a day, 3 webhook addresses and 3 assistants; Pro 25, 50,000, 20 and 10; Team 50, 100,000, 40 and 25 for each member.

Two-step sign-in asks for a six-digit code from an authenticator app after you sign in with Google. Someone with your Google password still can't get into your Video Controls Plus account without it. It is optional for everyone and on for every staff account. You turn it on in Account → Security on the website, and the extension follows it: see The extension.

It takes about two minutes. You need your phone and somewhere to keep ten recovery codes. Open Security and press Set up two-step. Scan the QR code with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Authy or any app that reads these codes. Can't scan? Type the setup key into the app as a time-based key. Type the code the app shows for Video Controls Plus and press Turn on two-step. The code changes every 30 seconds, so use the one showing now. Save the ten recovery codes: Copy all or Download .txt, then press I've saved them.

A recovery code gets you in when you don't have your phone. Each one works once, and looks like k7m2p-x9qr4; type it with or without the dash. We keep only a scrambled copy, so the setup screen is the only time you see them. Security shows how many you have left, and warns you when you're down to three. Make new codes replaces the whole set: the ten old codes stop working the moment the new ones appear. It needs your authenticator code and a sign-in from the last ten minutes.
Sign in with Google as before, then type the code from your authenticator. After several codes that don't match, you wait ten minutes, or use a recovery code.

After a code you can tick Remember this browser for 7 days. It starts unticked; tick it only on a browser that's yours. That browser then skips the code at sign-in until the seven days are up. Visiting doesn't extend them. A remembered browser still asks for a code before it shows an access key or a webhook signing secret, and staff pages ask every time. Security lists each remembered browser with the time it stops skipping the code. Forget one, or Forget all browsers, and each asks for a code next time. Signing out on a browser forgets it too.

On the code screen, choose Lost your phone? and Use a recovery code instead. Type one of your codes. You're in for this session, and two-step stays on. We email you that a recovery code was used. Press Add a new phone straight away and scan the new QR code. Showing a key or a secret needs a code from an authenticator, so do this before you need one. Lost your phone and every recovery code? Write to us from the email address on your account through the contact page. We check that it's you with questions about your own library, then turn two-step off so you can sign in with Google and set it up again. We email you when it's done. We never turn it off for a message from any other address.

New phone: type a code from your current phone, then scan the new QR code. The old phone's codes stop working. Turn off: type a code from your authenticator and press Turn it off. Signing in needs only Google again, and your recovery codes and remembered browsers go too. Staff accounts keep two-step on.
documents.s: A new phone, or turning it off

documents.t: Security lists each time you signed in on the website or connected the extension on a browser, with how: Google, Google and two-step, a remembered browser, a recovery code or an extension connect. Sign out everywhere else ends every other session. It also disconnects the extension on those browsers until you connect it again.

The extension has no password and no sign-in of its own. It connects to your website account: it opens the website, you sign in, compare the short code and press Connect this browser (how connecting works). With two-step on, you type your code (or use a remembered browser) before you approve. Seven days. With two-step on, a connected extension stays trusted for 7 days from when you connected it, never longer. Then it shows Connect again, and you connect it the same way to keep syncing. Speed control and everything that works without an account carry on in between. Turned on later. Turn two-step on after connecting, and that connection isn't trusted. Connect the extension again. Removing a browser. Remove a browser under The extension on Security, or with the API, and the extension on that browser is signed out. It shows Connect again. Two-step sign-in never asks for a code inside the extension. Every code is typed on the website.

A webhook tells your server the moment something changes in your library. Save a note and we send a short signed message to an address of yours. By default it says what happened, to which item and when. What you wrote stays in your library unless you tick Include what was written. A message goes out for a change made anywhere: in the extension, on the website, with an access key or by an assistant.

On the website, open Account → Other apps and press Add an address. Paste an https:// address on your server, and a description if you like, such as "Obsidian inbox". Tick the events to send. Each part has an Every … event box that ticks all of its events at once. Leave Include what was written off if the address is shared with other people. Press Add address, then copy the signing secret. It starts with whsec_. Adding an address needs a sign-in from the last ten minutes, and your two-step code when two-step sign-in is on. We email you that it was added; the email doesn't contain the secret. We only send to addresses the internet can reach, and we check this again before every message: https:// only, on port 443 or 8443, up to 2,048 characters, with no name or password in it; not a private or local network address, and not one of our own addresses; a host name that resolves.

Bookmarks: bookmark.saved, bookmark.updated, bookmark.removed Notes: note.saved, note.updated, note.deleted Collections: collection.created, collection.updated, collection.deleted, collection.video_added, collection.video_removed Flashcards: flashcard.created, flashcard.updated, flashcard.reviewed, flashcard.deleted Learning paths: learning_path.created, learning_path.updated, learning_path.deleted, learning_path.video_added, learning_path.video_completed, learning_path.video_removed Watch history: watch_history.added, watch_history.removed Watch later: watch_later.added, watch_later.removed Transcripts: transcript.saved, transcript.deleted Screenshots: screenshot.saved, screenshot.deleted Settings and shortcuts: settings.updated Devices: device.added, device.removed Your address: webhook.test, from Send test An updated event means something you wrote changed. Activity doesn't count: a review moves a card's schedule and sends flashcard.reviewed, not flashcard.updated, and a path's minutes watched send nothing. Watch history sends added the first time you watch a video and removed when it is removed, never as your place in the video moves. Watch parties, site fixes and feature requests send no events.

Each message is a POST with a JSON body and three headers: POST /hooks/vcp HTTP/1.1 Content-Type: application/json User-Agent: VideoControlsPlus-Webhooks/1.0 webhook-id: msg_3f1c9a7e52b84d0e9a6c41b27d58e0f3 webhook-timestamp: 1795252443 webhook-signature: v1,Sf2fD3s8K3tN/GbULA6VRokN3DtARXbma24DDern6WY= {"type":"note.saved","timestamp":"2026-11-21T09:14:03.512Z","data":{"id":"0b6f3c1e-8a2d-4f5b-9c7e-1d2a3b4c5d6e","video_id":"dQw4w9WgXcQ","platform":"youtube","occurred_at":"2026-11-21T09:14:03.512418+00:00"}} data holds the item's id, its video_id and platform when it is about a video, and occurred_at. For settings.updated, id is your account's. Fetch the item with the API when you need the rest of it. With Include what was written on, data also carries a short list for each part: Part Added to data Bookmarks label, note, color, position_seconds Notes content, category, tags Collections name, description; for videos, collection_id and video_title Flashcards front, back, tags Learning paths title, description; for videos, path_id, video_title, notes Watch history video_title, channel_name Watch later video_title, priority, notes Transcripts language, format Screenshots position_seconds, width, height Settings and shortcuts changed: ["settings"], ["shortcuts"] or both Devices device_name, browser A transcript's text never goes out in a message, ticked or not. Read it with a key from transcript_texts. The same note, with the box ticked: { "type": "note.saved", "timestamp": "2026-11-21T09:14:03.512Z", "data": { "id": "0b6f3c1e-8a2d-4f5b-9c7e-1d2a3b4c5d6e", "video_id": "dQw4w9WgXcQ", "platform": "youtube", "occurred_at": "2026-11-21T09:14:03.512418+00:00", "content": "Chorus comes back at 1:43. Use it for the timing exercise.", "category": "action", "tags": ["music-theory"] } } A settings change, and the test message: {"type":"settings.updated","timestamp":"2026-11-21T10:02:41.090Z","data":{"id":"6a1f0c52-3b7d-4e8a-9f21-0c4d5e6b7a89","occurred_at":"2026-11-21T10:02:41.090137+00:00","changed":["shortcuts"]}} {"type":"webhook.test","timestamp":"2026-11-21T10:05:12.334Z","data":{"message":"Test event"}}

Messages are signed with Standard Webhooks, so any Standard Webhooks library reads the secret as it is. To check by hand: Join webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and the raw body, exactly as received, with a . between each. Take your secret without whsec_, base64-decode it, and compute an HMAC-SHA256 of that text with it. Base64-encode the result. It must equal one of the v1, values in webhook-signature, which holds one or more separated by spaces. Refuse a timestamp more than five minutes from your clock, so an old message can't be sent again. Parse the JSON only after the check passes. A body parsed and serialised again no longer matches its signature. The samples below can be checked against the message above with this secret, made for this page only: whsec_dmNwLWRvY3Mtc2FtcGxlLXNlY3JldC0zMi1ieXRlcyE= Its correct signature is v1,Sf2fD3s8K3tN/GbULA6VRokN3DtARXbma24DDern6WY=. Your own secret is on Other apps.
documents.s: Checking a message came from us

documents.t: import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto'; import { createServer } from 'node:http'; /** True when the message was signed with `secret` in the last five minutes. */ export function isFromVideoControlsPlus(secret, headers, rawBody, nowSeconds = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)) { const id = headers['webhook-id']; const timestamp = headers['webhook-timestamp']; const signatures = headers['webhook-signature']; if (!id || !timestamp || !signatures || !/^\d+$/.test(timestamp)) return false; if (Math.abs(nowSeconds - Number(timestamp)) > 300) return false; const key = Buffer.from(secret.replace(/^whsec_/, ''), 'base64'); const expected = createHmac('sha256', key).update(`${id}.${timestamp}.${rawBody}`).digest(); return signatures.split(' ').some((entry) => { const [version, value] = entry.split(','); if (version !== 'v1' || !value) return false; const given = Buffer.from(value, 'base64'); return given.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(given, expected); }); } createServer((req, res) => { const chunks = []; req.on('data', (chunk) => chunks.push(chunk)); req.on('end', () => { const rawBody = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8'); if (!isFromVideoControlsPlus(process.env.VCP_WEBHOOK_SECRET, req.headers, rawBody)) { res.writeHead(400).end(); return; } const message = JSON.parse(rawBody); res.writeHead(204).end(); // Handle message.type after answering, so a slow job never runs past the ten-second wait. }); }).listen(8443);

import base64 import hashlib import hmac import time def is_from_video_controls_plus(secret, headers, raw_body, now_seconds=None): """True when the message was signed with `secret` in the last five minutes.""" msg_id = headers.get("webhook-id") timestamp = headers.get("webhook-timestamp") signatures = headers.get("webhook-signature") if not msg_id or not timestamp or not signatures or not timestamp.isdigit(): return False now = int(time.time()) if now_seconds is None else now_seconds if abs(now - int(timestamp)) > 300: return False key = base64.b64decode(secret.removeprefix("whsec_")) signed = f"{msg_id}.{timestamp}.".encode() + raw_body expected = base64.b64encode(hmac.new(key, signed, hashlib.sha256).digest()).decode() for entry in signatures.split(" "): version, _, value = entry.partition(",") if version == "v1" and hmac.compare_digest(value, expected): return True return False Pass raw_body as the bytes you received: request.get_data() in Flask, await request.body() in FastAPI.

Answer with any 2xx within ten seconds. We don't follow redirects, so a 3xx counts as a failure. A message that fails is tried again 5 seconds later, then after 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 5 hours, 10 hours and 10 hours: eight tries over about 27 hours. Every try of one message keeps the same webhook-id, so store the ids you've handled and skip a repeat. An address is turned off when it answers 410 Gone, or when its messages have failed for five days in a row. We email you when that happens, with its last answer. Press Turn back on in Other apps when your server is ready.

Each address in Other apps has these, beside the events it sends: Send test sends webhook.test. It shows in the delivery log when your server answers. Pause stops sending. Nothing piles up to send later; messages from the moment you press Turn back on go out. Delivery log lists the last messages, newest first, with the result, the time it took and the number of tries. Send again sends one again with the same webhook-id. Remove stops everything for that address.

Show signing secret works within ten minutes of signing in, with your two-step code when it's on. Replace secret makes a new one. For 24 hours each message carries both signatures, new first, so switch your server to the new secret before then and no message fails in between.
Free holds 3 webhook addresses, Pro 20 and Team 40 for each member. When you're at the limit, remove one, or move to a plan with more on Plans.

A browser extension that adds playback controls to HTML5 video. It works on any site that plays a standard video, with extra tools on YouTube, Netflix and LinkedIn, and it ships for Chrome, Edge and Firefox. To add it, see Install.

Press ] or [ for 0.1x steps, or drag the slider in the widget up to 4x. For anything faster, type the speed into the widget's custom input or the Custom Speed boxes on the General tab in Settings, up to 16x. Speed control works without an account. See Speed control.

documents.t: An A-B loop replays the stretch between two points you set; it needs a connected account. Press Ctrl + Alt + A at the start and Ctrl + Alt + B at the end, and the video plays that part until you clear it with Ctrl + Alt + Backspace. See A-B loop.

Yes. Connect an account to save timestamped notes and export them as Markdown, text or JSON from the widget's Tools tab. Ctrl + Alt + O adds a bookmark at the current moment without an account. documents.t: Open a video on YouTube, Udemy, Vimeo or any other site with a standard video. Press ] to go 0.1x faster, and keep pressing until you reach 4x. Press [ to go 0.1x slower. Press = to go back to your default speed. Press Ctrl + Alt + 4 to jump straight to 2x. That's speed control, and it needs no account. The same keyboard does a lot more than speed: , and . step the video one frame at a time, and Ctrl + Alt + P puts it in a Picture-in-Picture window, before you connect an account.
The widget is the floating control panel on the page. Click it to open it, and drag it where you want it. Press Esc or Ctrl + Alt + H to hide the widget, and press again to bring it back.

Video Controls Plus is a browser extension that adds playback controls to HTML5 video. You control the video player the way you want it, on any site that plays a standard video, and you get special tools on YouTube, Netflix and LinkedIn. It ships for Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

Speed comes first. Press ] to go 0.1x faster and [ to go 0.1x slower, and that works without an account. It does a lot more than change the speed: you can loop a part of a video with an A-B loop, boost the audio up to 400%, adjust brightness, contrast and saturation, save a frame as a screenshot, and keep notes with the timestamp. Without an account, you have speed, presets, frame step, Picture-in-Picture, share timestamp, browser-local bookmarks and the widget. The A-B loop, audio boost, filters, screenshots, notes and auto-skip open after you connect an account. Version 16.3.0 adds a set of tools to the widget and to Settings. Comfort, the Study timer, Zoom & fit, the Automation section, watch limits and Focus Mode need no account. Looks and effects, audio tools, capture and export, the library tools and watch parties need a connected account, and each page below says which part needs what.
